exposure: donation stool consistency (Bristol Stool Form Scale score)
donor antibiotic use (3-12 months before donation)
outcome: resolution of diarrhoea associated with C difficile infection
cohort: The cohort consisted of faeces donors (who fulfilled national criteria and delivered donations to Aarhus University Hospital, Denmark) and corresponding recipients treated with one-dose Faecal Microbiota Transplantation for primary or recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection.
finding: Antibiotic use 3-12 months before donation decreased the effectiveness of Faecal Microbiota Transplantation (FMT), while donations with a Bristol Stool Form Scale score of 4 and 5 or above showed improved FMT effectiveness compared to a score of 3.
mod_finding: Donor birth mode did not affect Faecal Microbiota Transplantation (FMT) outcomes.
